components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Compact violet command for loading a player or running analysis.
components.css: .ds-button { height: 40px; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 4px; background: var(--violet, #8873ee); color: #080b12; font: 750 15px Outfit, sans-serif; padding: 0 17px; transition: transform 140ms cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1), background-color 160ms ease; } .ds-button:hover { background: #9b88ef; } .ds-button:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid rgba(136,115,238,.35); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-button:active { transform: scale(.97); }

components.name: Input Field
components.description: Native dark field used for Riot ID, filters, and analysis inputs.
components.css: .ds-label { display: grid; gap: 6px; color: #c2cad4; font: 600 12px Outfit, sans-serif; } .ds-input { height: 40px; border: 1px solid rgba(197,211,228,.28); border-radius: 4px; background: #101925; color: #f3f0e9; caret-color: #8873ee; padding: 0 12px; transition: border-color 160ms ease, background-color 160ms ease, outline-color 160ms ease; } .ds-input:focus-visible { border-color: #8873ee; outline: 3px solid rgba(136,115,238,.2); background: #182333; }

components.name: Tab Rail
components.description: Text navigation with a moving selection rule.
components.css: .ds-tabs { position: relative; display: flex; gap: 28px; border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(197,211,228,.28); background: #060a10; } .ds-tab { min-height: 58px; border: 0; background: transparent; color: #9ba8b8; font: 600 14px Outfit, sans-serif; } .ds-tab:hover,.ds-tab:focus-visible,.ds-tab.ds-active { color: #f3f0e9; } .ds-rule { position: absolute; bottom: -1px; left: 0; width: 64px; height: 3px; background: #8873ee; }

components.description: TFT-native hex for activated trait thresholds only.

narrative.overview: TFT Tracker is a post-game review desk: part tournament broadcast, part analyst notebook, and part polished desktop application. It is built for repeated personal analysis, so expression comes from composition, typography, and game-specific data language rather than decorative chrome. The system alternates dense ruled analysis fields with one decisive mineral-paper ledger surface. Key performance numbers stand in open space. Repeated cards are reserved for repeated objects such as comps; the page itself is organized as connected editorial bands.
keyCharacteristics: An asymmetric player masthead with the tactician integrated into identity.
A mineral-paper twenty-game ledger as the signature first-viewport surface.
Open, tabular performance numerals without nested metric cards.
Flat ink surfaces divided by precise rules instead of glow or broad shadow.
Blue placements for first through fourth and red placements for fifth through eighth.
Fast, interruptible interaction feedback with a reduced-motion equivalent.

rules.name: The Identity/Data Split Rule
rules.body: Violet identifies the product and current selection. Cobalt, stepped blues, and stepped reds encode player data.

rules.name: The Paper Is Earned Rule
rules.body: Mineral paper appears only where the interface changes reading mode: the match ledger, the insight lead, and onboarding.

rules.name: The Honest State Rule
rules.body: Cached data, unavailable sources, validation errors, and empty results remain visible and plainly written.

rules.name: The Numeral Authority Rule
rules.body: Primary statistics are large, tabular, and left aligned. Their labels explain them without competing for attention.

rules.name: The One Edge Rule
rules.body: A surface may use a divider or a border, never a border plus a broad shadow.

rules.name: The No Glow Rule
rules.body: Colored halos, chromatic shadows, shiny accents, and blurred atmosphere do not belong in the application.

dos: Do use editorial bands and rules to organize primary analysis.
Do let important performance numerals occupy open space.
Do reserve mineral paper for meaningful changes in reading mode.
Do preserve exact blue and red placement semantics across views.
Do keep controls native, compact, keyboard accessible, and visibly focused.
Do use 140-220ms motion for state, orientation, and feedback.
Do label cached, unavailable, and incomplete data honestly.
donts: Don't rebuild the page as a uniform grid of rounded cards.
Don't use glow, glossy gradients, glass, purple atmosphere, or shiny borders.
Don't turn metadata, tags, or scope values into clouds of pills.
Don't use gaming fonts, neon cyberpunk styling, or Discord-bot visual language.
Don't use hexagons outside trait and board-specific contexts.
Don't add ambient motion, decorative floating, or long page transitions.
Don't invent recommendations, global comparisons, or statistics the data does not provide.
